New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 6 in room_progress_event_0 ($7C7C-$7C82). Seven-byte room-progress event 0: room 0, threshold 21, mutable target pointer $6DD1, reset value $40, threshold value $00 and message/room selector $FF. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_1 ($7C83-$7C89). Seven-byte room-progress event 1: room 0, threshold 21, mutable target pointer $121F, reset value $00, threshold value $FF and message/room selector $FF. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_2 ($7C8A-$7C90). Seven-byte room-progress event 2: room 0, threshold 21, mutable target pointer $BC30, reset value $00, threshold value $FF and message/room selector $01. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_3 ($7C91-$7C97). Seven-byte room-progress event 3: room 1, threshold 254, mutable target pointer $72A6, reset value $40, threshold value $00 and message/room selector $02. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_4 ($7C98-$7C9E). Seven-byte room-progress event 4: room 1, threshold 254, mutable target pointer $BC31, reset value $00, threshold value $FF and message/room selector $02. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_5 ($7C9F-$7CA5). Seven-byte room-progress event 5: room 2, threshold 64, mutable target pointer $6E03, reset value $40, threshold value $00 and message/room selector $03. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_6 ($7CA6-$7CAC). Seven-byte room-progress event 6: room 3, threshold 20, mutable target pointer $6E24, reset value $40, threshold value $00 and message/room selector $04. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_7 ($7CAD-$7CB3). Seven-byte room-progress event 7: room 4, threshold 100, mutable target pointer $6E31, reset value $40, threshold value $00 and message/room selector $05. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_8 ($7CB4-$7CBA). Seven-byte room-progress event 8: room 6, threshold 90, mutable target pointer $72E8, reset value $41, threshold value $01 and message/room selector $07. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 0 in room_progress_event_9 ($7CBB-$7CC1). Seven-byte room-progress event 9: room 7, threshold 35, mutable target pointer $6DBC, reset value $40, threshold value $00 and message/room selector $08. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.

Offset 6 in room_progress_event_9 ($7CBB-$7CC1). Seven-byte room-progress event 9: room 7, threshold 35, mutable target pointer $6DBC, reset value $40, threshold value $00 and message/room selector $08. New-game initialization restores the reset value; crossing the threshold writes its replacement.
Offset 0 in wave_actor_x_positions ($7CC2-$7CCB). Ten half-resolution X positions for the room-ending wave. The wave counter indexes the overlapping base $7CC1 beginning at one.
Offset 9 in wave_actor_x_positions ($7CC2-$7CCB). Ten half-resolution X positions for the room-ending wave. The wave counter indexes the overlapping base $7CC1 beginning at one.
Offset 0 in wave_actor_y_positions ($7CCC-$7CD5). Ten Y positions paired with the wave X table. The wave counter indexes the overlapping base $7CCB beginning at one.

Offset 0 in wave_table_tail ($7CD6-$7CD6). Zero byte following the ten wave Y coordinates and before the raster-split routine. The wave allocator stops at counter eleven, so this byte is outside its coordinate reads.

Preserve X/Y and process sorted vertical sprite-slice events from $DE and $D1. At each reached line, change that sprite's Y and increment its pointer to the next cached slice. Wait near the next event or schedule an interrupt two lines before it; when no earlier event remains, schedule the status body at raster $FA. Restore the saved processor state through the interrupt return path.

Immediate operand of LDA at $7D02, written with six by the new-game initializer. The split-raster body writes this colour to sprite-six colour register $D02D when the hardware Y differs from the retained clipped position. It is a self-modified colour value, not an instruction entry.
Eight offsets zero, two, four through fourteen, indexed by sprite slot when the split body selects the corresponding VIC X/Y register pair.

Choose the animation at $7B72 and enter the shared diagonal-movement controller. Its startup phase chooses signed horizontal/vertical speeds toward the player, excluding the equal-two-speed combination; subsequent updates can steer toward the player.
Choose animation $7BA2 and share the diagonal-movement controller at $7D4D.
If health is below four, enter the falling controller with speed four; otherwise use the ordinary animated movement path at $7DBD.
Advance this actor's animation, move it when the animation permits, and stage its component sprites through $AB0F.
Refresh the actor's bounds, calculate signed player/actor separation through $B5C7 and return its absolute magnitude in A/Y. Carry indicates the sign conversion used by callers.
Advance animation and, when the start-grace and actor flag tests allow, periodically steer its velocity toward the player. Apply movement and stage the actor's sprites.
Count twenty eligible updates before checking proximity. Within the vertical and horizontal windows, reverse the horizontal and vertical velocities whose signs point away from the player.
Run the common spawn-placement check; when it succeeds, put the actor into mode $81 and return carry clear.
Convert the player's world X to half resolution, retain it in $68 and form the facing-dependent rectangle for shape X through $7E69.

Use the four pose-bound arrays at $7EBC, $7ED1, $7EE6 and $7EFB to build top/bottom and half-resolution left/right bounds. Reflect the horizontal offsets for facing and clamp the relevant overflow cases.
Offset 0 in player_pose_top_offsets ($7EBC-$7ED0). Twenty-one signed vertical top offsets indexed by player collision shape; added to the supplied Y by $7E69.
Offset 0 in player_pose_bottom_offsets ($7ED1-$7EE5). Twenty-one bottom offsets paired with the pose top-offset table. Vertical collision clamps use this same array.
Offset 0 in player_pose_left_offsets ($7EE6-$7EFA). Twenty-one signed half-X left offsets. Facing reflection exchanges/adjusts these with the right offsets around the pose anchor.
Offset 0 in player_pose_right_offsets ($7EFB-$7F0F). Twenty-one half-X right offsets paired with $7EE6 for collision rectangles and horizontal clamping.
For rooms below eight, select the handler word from $749E using twice the room plus the supplied byte offset A, and jump through $1A/$1B.
Build the current player's pose rectangle and dispatch the first bank of eight room callbacks with offset zero.
Build the current player's pose rectangle and dispatch the second bank of eight room callbacks with offset $10.
AND persistent flags $0140/$0141. When the result is zero, clear bit five in this room's second state byte at $1241+room-state-base.
Set animation gate $02C1 to $E0 when state four has reached its target and $1208 is zero; clear the gate otherwise.
Use the player's half-X threshold $87 and room byte $BC30 to request the state-opening path or the closing path for the room's first state.
Outside doorway states 10/11, use the player's Y and half-X rectangle to request this room's first state to open or close, subject to its timer and $BC31 gate.
Outside doorway states, test the player's upper-room rectangle and request the first state to open when reached, or to close when the horizontal test fails.
Publish the room animation gate when state four reaches its target. Once $1208 is nonzero and the wave flag is clear, start the scripted wave through $A19A.

Walk geometry contacts for the player's rectangle and compare their pointers with the selected seventeen-byte record's stored contact. Return a bit mask distinguishing that contact from other contacts, ignoring the special $6F93 pointer.
Set room-attack code $44 for a Hammerfist punch, then enter the shared interaction-list search at $804D.
Set room-attack code $44 for a Metalisis kick, sharing the contact-pointer match and callback dispatch at $804D.
Select attack code $84 and enter the room's seven-byte interaction-list search.

Select attack code $46. Search this room's interaction records for either stored contact-pointer match, then jump to its handler with the record's value in A. Return carry set when the list is empty or no contact matches.

Check whether the actor can occupy its authored position without intersecting the player. Depending on scheduler flags, reset the record, disable a one-shot spawn or position it at a room-entry point and request a corresponding door state. Return carry set when placement must be refused or deferred.

Discard the suspended caller's return, animate the player disintegration by clearing cached sprite bands, then display game over. Convert the BCD score into six digits, insert a qualifying score among five rows and accept three initials with directional edges and fire. Initials YCY patch the F3 handler's branch opcode to enable its room-advance path before returning to the title loop.
Inline text argument for $1CF0: screen offset $0151, followed by the zero-terminated string 'O[K['. The printer resumes at $82A1; ASCII [ is a font-specific display character.
Resume after the high-score heading and select colour one for the inline initials-entry instructions.
Inline text argument for $1CF0: screen offset $019C, followed by the zero-terminated string 'MAKE YOUR MARK[[['. The printer resumes at $82BA; ASCII [ is a font-specific display character.

Highlight the inserted score row, poll directional press edges to wrap the chosen initial through A to the following glyph, and accept each of three positions on fire. After the third initial, clear its highlight and check the YCY sequence before returning to the title.
Eight colours cycled by the game-over disintegration loop using its countdown's low three bits.
Clear three bytes beginning at offset A in each of four cached player images at $2B40, $2C00, $3040 and $3100. Return Y at the original offset.

Wait until sprite slots 1-4 are available, allocate eligible scheduled actors and walk the ordered active-slot list. Remove retired entries, dispatch death/pickup and doorway modes separately, process recoil before the actor's ordinary update callback, then mark the staged secondary sprites ready.

Scan nine-byte records from the pointer in object bytes 22/23, skipping entries whose persistent state is set. Copy position, velocity magnitudes, movement-script pointer and animation into the actor slot, refresh its bounds and return carry clear. A terminator or null script pointer refuses the spawn.

Advance animation, then execute duration/control pairs from the actor's movement script. Decode two-bit signed vertical and horizontal directions using its stored magnitudes, apply movement and stop a blocked duration. $FF retires through the special actor path; $FE removes the actor directly. Stage the current component sprites afterward.
Refuse initialization while saved Y $13CF is zero. Otherwise initialize the scripted actor, replace its coordinates with the saved $13CD-$13CF position and consume that saved position.

Advance the requested inward-facing pose, or interpret controls while the player faces the scenery. Horizontal input leaves that pose; fire with up enters state 10 or 11 according to the depth flag, while fire with down selects state 9 when the player is at the front depth. Up without fire can request a character change.
Put A in the player state $59, reset the action step $5A and clear the three attack-contact markers $A1-$A3 before returning.

Walk four scheduled actor slots before leaving the room. Move actors away from screen edges or finish recoil over bounded substeps, adjust special doorway modes and write mutable coordinates, facing and flags back to their source records. Temporary/unscheduled slots are skipped.
Four twenty-five-byte central status images: one colour and three eight-cell glyph rows each. The portrait updater chooses a multiple-of-25 offset and can alternate a warning image with image zero.
Offset 1 in master_portrait_glyphs ($86DC-$873E). Central status portrait/message glyph images. $A1D4 selects an image and copies three eight-cell rows; the table retains its packed selection layout.
Offset 9 in master_portrait_glyphs ($86DC-$873E). Central status portrait/message glyph images. $A1D4 selects an image and copies three eight-cell rows; the table retains its packed selection layout.

Offset 17 in master_portrait_glyphs ($86DC-$873E). Central status portrait/message glyph images. $A1D4 selects an image and copies three eight-cell rows; the table retains its packed selection layout.

Offset 48 in master_portrait_glyphs ($86DC-$873E). Central status portrait/message glyph images. $A1D4 selects an image and copies three eight-cell rows; the table retains its packed selection layout.

Offset 96 in master_portrait_glyphs ($86DC-$873E). Central status portrait/message glyph images. $A1D4 selects an image and copies three eight-cell rows; the table retains its packed selection layout.
Store A into the music entry's writable request operand at $EEAF. The IRQ's selected music updater processes the request.

Convert player X to half resolution, subtract $14 and divide by sixteen. Reject a result outside eight columns; otherwise use that column index in the shared randomized platform-based spawn path at $875F.

Choose one of eight seventeen-byte platform records through $8792. Refuse the spawn when its leading byte is below $1C; otherwise select a randomized Y and corresponding X offset and refresh actor bounds. The intended use of that leading-byte test is unresolved.
Offset 0 in platform_spawn_record_offsets ($8792-$8799). Offsets of eight seventeen-byte moving-platform records, used by the randomized spawn initializer.
Offset 0 in platform_spawn_x_offsets ($879A-$87A1). Eight horizontal offsets paired with the platform selection for actor spawn placement.
Retain the state's low-five-bit position, add opening/request flags $60 and store it. A state at position zero also queues effect nine.
When the state's position is nonzero and equals its target, set closing/request flags $A0. Positions at least four also queue effect nine.

Sum active actors' low-nibble sprite costs and find free slots while the total is below four. In the scripted-wave mode, spawn timed temporary actors from the wave coordinate tables and mark completion after its final entry. Otherwise ask the room scheduler for an eligible object. Append each accepted slot to the ordered actor list.

Apply the current animation delay, character-change flash and energy checks, then dispatch the player state through $8CE2. Idle movement uses candidate coordinates, geometry checks and the walk pose/delay tables; active actions use their own step handlers. State-dependent geometry checks can redirect an action into forced movement.

Read mirrored VIC raster/control registers and CIA2 timer-register mirrors. On the low-raster path, differing timer comparisons can write Y into the high operand byte at $8A63 of the standing-pose jump. The intended purpose of this timing-dependent patch is unknown.

Set walk-phase bit one according to character, mark the player stationary and clear forced-redraw and transition markers. Enter the common pose-selection path at $89A3 with the retained walk phase; this entry does not itself reset the animation-delay byte.
High operand byte of the JMP at $8A61. The raster/timer guard at $8A2E can overwrite this byte with Y; ordinary standing-pose selection follows the assembled jump target.

Inspect the active character's energy. When empty, request a change if the other character has at least $20 energy; otherwise discard the immediate return address and enter the game-over path. An ongoing character-change flash postpones the empty-energy handling.

Forty-eight pose indices in six eight-step groups. The low four index bits select phase and character for ordinary walking. Forced-motion state adds $10 or $20 to select the alternate forward/backward pose groups before the layered renderer reads this table.

Thirty-two horizontal displacement magnitudes indexed by phase and character, with an additional $10 bank selected while the reverse-motion counter is active. The walking code adds or subtracts the selected byte from candidate X according to facing/transition state.

Sixteen animation intervals indexed by the low four phase/character bits. Hammerfist's eight entries are four ticks and Metalisis's eight are five ticks. The player updater compares elapsed low ticks with the retained interval before advancing its pose.
Return after the walk-delay table selection. This is the final RTS of the walking interval helper.

Decode the sampled direction and fire bits into walking, ducking, character change or attack states. Fire plus direction selects character-specific attacks; three fresh fire presses without a direction request the inward-facing pose. Up changes character only when its energy and flash tests permit it.

Require up held and a fresh up edge, no existing change flash and at least $21 energy in the other character. Set the six-step flash and forced redraw, queue effect ten and consume the up edge. Insufficient energy still consumes that edge.

Test the facing-specific forward direction while fire is held. Consume the direction/fire edges and mark the player stationary; Hammerfist enters horizontal punch, while Metalisis initializes flicflac at step two and retains the starting Y. Dispatch immediately or use the alternate pose path according to walk phase.
Toggle horizontal facing, set the turnaround flag and six-tick delay, mark the player stationary and force a fresh pose. Choose the appropriate character's turnaround image.
Two pose indices selected by the Hammerfist turnaround handler.
Two pose indices selected for Metalisis when the shared turnaround setup chooses her character branch.
Two held-crouch pose indices indexed directly by character zero/one. Releasing down uses the following standing-pose table at $8CCD.

Four standing pose indices selected when down is released from crouching. Character chooses the first/second entry, and walk-phase bit two selects the other pair. The held crouch itself reads the two preceding entries at $8CCB.
Double state $59, read its handler word from $8CE2 and jump indirectly through $1A/$1B. The selected handler returns to the caller of this dispatcher.

Fifteen handler words indexed by twice $59. Entry zero is null because idle movement is handled before this dispatch; entries 1-14 implement ducking, attacks, flicflac, forced movement, scenery actions, doorway movement and recovery.
High byte of the null idle-state handler word at $8CE2. Active action dispatch reads adjacent low/high bytes after doubling the state index.

Keep the player in the crouched pose while down is held. Count fresh fire presses during the crouch and cycle the two equipped weapons on the second press. Releasing down ends the action and restores the idle state.

Advance the horizontal-kick pose sequence. During its contact steps, test the directed attack rectangle against room interactions and actors, retaining contact markers so the same action can suppress repeated hits. Return to idle at the sequence end.
Twelve pose indices for six horizontal-kick steps, with the walk-phase/facing selector choosing each step's paired image.
Twelve delay entries paired with the horizontal-kick poses at $8DDD.

Advance the horizontal-punch sequence and test its contact frames against the room and actors. A selected laser with charge can launch a horizontal shot at step four. A charged piston punch can consume charge and repeat part of the sequence while forward plus fire remains held.
Twelve pose indices for the horizontal punch's six action steps, including the repeating piston segment.
Twelve delays paired with the horizontal-punch pose sequence.

Advance the upward-punch poses, test the upward contact rectangle and actor hits, and launch an upward laser on its firing step when the laser is selected and charged. Finish by restoring idle movement.
Ten pose indices for five upward-punch steps, selected in pairs by the action's pose bit.
Ten delays paired with the upward-punch poses at $8FA2.
Advance the downward-punch poses and directed contact checks. A charged selected laser can fire downward at step eight. Restore the idle state after the last pose.
Fourteen pose indices for the downward punch's seven action steps.
Fourteen delays paired with the downward-punch poses at $904E.

Handle the inward-facing down/fire action. Inspect the object or activation rectangle in front of the player, perform its interaction and animate the headbutt. At a recharge point, subtract score while adding energy; crossing the energy limit follows the explosion and character-change branch. The ordinary completion path advances the action poses and restores idle state.
Twelve pose indices for the inward-facing headbutt action's six steps, including its recharge hold.
Twelve delays paired with the inward-facing headbutt/recharge pose sequence.
Clear player state $59 and return when the headbutt/recharge pose sequence reaches its completion step.
Select the second half of the doorway pose/delay arrays and enter the shared depth-movement handler at $91C3.

Run the doorway/depth movement sequence, checking the relevant geometry and state flags before progressing. Change sprite priority and player visibility during the movement, update the inward/depth flags at its milestones and return to idle when the chosen sequence completes.
Offset 0 in depth_action_poses ($9303-$9342). Two thirty-two-byte doorway/depth pose sequences. The shared handler selects offset zero or $20 and indexes poses by action step and character.
Offset 48 in depth_action_poses ($9303-$9342). Two thirty-two-byte doorway/depth pose sequences. The shared handler selects offset zero or $20 and indexes poses by action step and character.
Offset 0 in depth_action_delays ($9343-$9382). Delays paired with the two doorway pose sequences at $9303.
Offset 48 in depth_action_delays ($9343-$9382). Delays paired with the two doorway pose sequences at $9303.
Run three recovery poses, clear the flicflac flag $A7 and restore idle movement at the end.
Six pose indices for the three-step recovery handlers, selected by action step and pose bit.
Six delays paired with the three-step recovery poses at $93AC.

Walk the saved flicflac history backward, restoring coordinates and poses. The special reset flag can restore the room-entry position instead. At the history end, leave the flicflac state or enter forced movement according to the remaining motion flag.
Run the three-pose recovery sequence and restore idle state while retaining the flicflac flag.

Cancel the current player action and inward-facing state, select forced movement and examine floor geometry. A landing takes the floor-handling path; otherwise use the stored displacement/direction and countdown to continue the fall or recoil.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed three with vertical speed two, signing horizontal motion by facing before refreshing bounds.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed six with vertical speed one.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed two with vertical speed two.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed four with vertical speed one.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed two with vertical speed one.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed one with zero vertical velocity.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed two with zero vertical velocity.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed three with zero vertical velocity.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed six with zero vertical velocity.
Place the scheduled actor and select horizontal speed four with zero vertical velocity.
Refuse this spawn when both $02C3 and $02C4 have their high bit set; otherwise use the horizontal-speed-two initializer.

Advance animation and derive the player's distance/facing relative to this actor. An idle actor can choose one of two attacks when close and vertically aligned, or choose a projectile response through $961E. Select the corresponding animation and dispatch one of four action handlers through $9616; otherwise track/move toward the player.
Four animation pointers selected by the actor mode's low six bits in $9566.
High byte of the first animation pointer in the actor attack table at $960E. The attack decision routine reads paired low/high bytes after doubling its mode index.
Four indirect handlers for the actor attack modes: two contact attacks and two collision-shape sequences.
High byte of the first attack-handler pointer at $9616. The mode dispatcher forms an indirect address from this table's adjacent low/high bytes.

Detect an active, travelling horizontal projectile approaching within the actor's distance/height window. Select response mode $42 or $43, reset its step counter and return carry set; otherwise leave the actor mode unchanged and return carry clear.
On action step one, run contact attack record zero through $A485, then stage the actor's sprites.
On action step one, run contact attack record five through $A485, then stage the actor's sprites.
Double the action-step counter to select a collision-shape pointer from $96BF, install it and stage the actor.
Select the second collision-shape sequence beginning eight bytes into $96BF, sharing the shape-installing path.
Ten collision-shape pointers for the two projectile-response sequences, including shared end poses.
High byte of the first collision-shape pointer in the response table at $96BF. Step handlers read the two adjacent bytes after doubling their step index.

Compare the actor's selected room state against its target. While waiting, stage its sprites and suppress affected publication slots; once reached, adjust its entry Y, clear the doorway mode, reset its animation tick and stage it normally.
Read the room-entry index from this actor's scheduler flags and add its fourth record byte to actor Y.
Subtract A from the active character's energy, clamping borrow to zero.
Refresh actor bounds, preserve Y and compare the player's current rectangle against the actor's vertical and full-resolution horizontal bounds. Return carry set for overlap.

For target byte $BC32 below $80, reject disallowed attack flags or add the low-six-bit attack amount and start an impact effect. Once the byte reaches $80, request the corresponding room state, record its event tick and queue effect $0E.
Add the current room-state base to A and enter the timed state-activation path at $AD2B.

Refuse most random draws and require a leading scheduled actor above the height threshold. Initialize this actor moving with opposite facing, copy the leading actor's coordinates and refresh its bounds.
Store the supplied mode through $9810 and return carry clear to the caller.
Put the actor into mode $F0, update its persistent scheduler record through $9810, and retain a nonzero event tick in $A9.
Store the low tick in $A9, substituting $FF when the tick is zero.
Store A as actor mode, set its retired flag, increment and cap its occurrence counter at $7F, and save the current time and mutable state back to its scheduler record when it has one. Preserve Y.
Copy the actor's X word and Y into $13D5-$13D7 for movement rollback.
Copy saved X word and Y at $13D5-$13D7 back to the current actor's position fields. This is the inverse of $983F.
Copy the actor's vertical bounds and convert each full-resolution horizontal bound into the geometry scanner's half-resolution range, clamping out-of-world values.
Five five-byte records consumed by $AD39: CIA keyboard selection mask, expected returned row, debounce-counter index and handler word. They bind F3, F5, F7, Space and F1 respectively.
Expected CIA keyboard-row byte for the F3 record at $98A6. The keyboard scanner compares this after selecting the row with that record's first byte.
Debounce-counter index zero in the F3 keyboard record. The scanner adds it to the counter base $13A9 before testing the three-sample threshold.
Low byte of the F3 handler pointer $98BF in the first keyboard-action record, paired with the high byte at $98AA.
High callback-address byte in the first five-byte keyboard record at $98A6. The keyboard scanner uses this layout for its F3, F5, F7, Space and F1 handlers.
Set weapon index $5B to zero and redraw its status indicator through $17D6.
Initially BEQ, taken after LDX zero to select no weapon. The YCY initials check writes BNE here; with Z still set, that patched branch falls through to the room-advance path at $98C3.
Increment route index $79 with wrap at $25, call $AFF1, force $3D to $FF and select no weapon. The high-score initials YCY change $98C1 from BEQ to BNE so F3 reaches this path after LDX zero.
Set weapon index $5B to one and redraw its status indicator. The keyboard action table binds this handler to F7.
Set weapon index $5B to two and redraw its status indicator. The keyboard action table binds this handler to F5.
Increment the current weapon index and wrap index three to one, then store it and redraw the indicator. The crouch/fire handler uses this to alternate laser and piston.
If the start-grace flag $93 and inward-facing flag $55 are both zero, set $55 to one. The Space keyboard callback uses this request rather than immediately drawing a pose.

Add $40 to the sound-mode byte $13B3, retain its top two bits and wrap $C0 to zero. Zero clears sound effects; entering $80 initializes and clears their driver, then queues effect $0E. This is the F1 keyboard callback.

Animate the effect in sprite slot zero when its staging slot is free. Use phase $80 to choose the bitmap, colour and multicolour setting and its duration; a zero image terminates the effect by clearing active Y coordinate $7F.
Image indices for the impact-animation phases. Phase zero overlaps the preceding RTS byte and is not an active animation frame.
Sixteen bitmap indices for nonzero impact-animation phases. The lookup base is $999A, overlapping the preceding RTS at inactive phase zero.
Packed colour, multicolour flag and low-three-bit duration values indexed by the impact phase in $80.

Select the room's rectangle range through $76A3/$76A4. Compare this slot's half-resolution X and Y against each four-byte rectangle at $6C32. Set its $0330 priority byte to $FF when the point lies inside a rectangle, or zero when no rectangle matches.

CPX #$D5 immediately before the flicflac history initializer at $99FF. It falls into that initializer, whose first LDX resets X and the comparison flags. The recovered control-flow entries start at $99FF; this two-byte prefix is retained code rather than a separate identified feature.

Store the first position, pose/delay and room in the six-point history arrays, select player state six and mark flicflac active. Clear landing/room-entry flags and mark moving platforms currently touched by the player, using the contact scanner for each platform in this room.

Calculate the current flicflac step's candidate displacement and dispatch its step handler through the word table at $9B55. The movement sequence retains coordinate/pose history for the rewind and recovery paths.

Save the next position in the flicflac history, commit candidate coordinates, select its pose and delay, and advance the two-byte step index. Holding up at the extension decision can continue into the high sequence; otherwise the low sequence reaches its earlier finish.
Offset 0 in flicflac_pose_pairs ($9AFB-$9B18). Thirty pose indices, paired by action step and the selected walk-phase bit for the flicflac and rewind renderer.
Offset 0 in flicflac_delay_pairs ($9B19-$9B36). Thirty delay values paired with the flicflac pose indices at $9AFB.

Offset 0 in flicflac_displacement_pairs ($9B37-$9B54). Fifteen signed horizontal/vertical displacement pairs indexed by the even action-step byte. The flicflac dispatcher combines them with facing and candidate position before its geometry checks.

Offset 1 in flicflac_displacement_pairs ($9B37-$9B54). Fifteen signed horizontal/vertical displacement pairs indexed by the even action-step byte. The flicflac dispatcher combines them with facing and candidate position before its geometry checks.
Offset 0 in flicflac_step_handlers ($9B55-$9B72). Fifteen handler words indexed by the even action-step value. The low and high flicflac paths share several contact/recovery handlers.
Offset 1 in flicflac_step_handlers ($9B55-$9B72). Fifteen handler words indexed by the even action-step value. The low and high flicflac paths share several contact/recovery handlers.
Select collision shape one and commit/check actor contact. A hit enters forced movement; otherwise advance the flicflac sequence with pose selector zero.

Test horizontal shape twenty, then vertical shape two and a six-damage actor attack. A wall/object hit starts impact and rewind; a vertical block restores the previous Y before recovery. On success advance using pose selector one.
Test shape three against horizontal geometry and actors. A contact triggers its impact/rewind path; otherwise advance using pose selector two.

Test vertical shape four and the one-pixel landing offset. A sufficiently large blocked descent selects rewind; a smaller block restores Y for recovery. Otherwise commit, check actor contact and floor landing, choosing a landing pose or advancing the sequence.
Consume the room-entry flag when set, test horizontal shape five and actor contact, and advance with pose selector four. A wall or actor collision enters the shared recovery/rewind setup.
Extend the history through $1F95, test shape seven horizontally and vertically and check actor contact. A collision starts rewind; otherwise enter the common step continuation.
Test shape eight in both axes, handle any pending geometry hazard and test the landing offset on a contact. Check actors and either retain its landing candidate for rewind or continue the action.

Test shape ten vertically and horizontally, commit coordinates and check the floor. A landing clears flicflac/state and chooses its landing pose; otherwise check actor contact and continue the sequence or forced motion.
Select collision shape zero, commit coordinates and check actor contact. A hit enters forced movement; otherwise continue the flicflac step sequence.
Test horizontal and vertical geometry with shape six, then actor contact. Contacts select the shared impact/rewind path; a clear step advances with pose selector five.
Add history points and test shape seven in both axes. A particular ceiling result selects impact ten; other geometry or actor contacts enter rewind, while a clear step continues the high sequence.

Use shape eight for the first vertical/horizontal tests. A blocked vertical path advances the action step and retests with shape nine, including hazard and landing-offset checks. Both paths check actors and either continue or begin rewind.

After a vertical block advances the action step, select collision shape nine and retest vertical/horizontal geometry. Retain impact twelve on a wall, process a geometry hazard, then test contact/landing and actor collisions before continuing or entering rewind.

Test shape ten, preserve the hazard response's action state, commit coordinates and test floor landing. On landing choose a pose and clear flicflac/state; otherwise continue or enter forced movement following actor contact.
Commit the candidate coordinates, temporarily test geometry one pixel below candidate Y using collision shape zero, then restore the player's Y and shape index while preserving the geometry result.

Average the candidate position with the stored history point before entering the shared rewind setup. Nonnegative A selects an impact effect; forced-motion collisions can also subtract energy. Update room interaction state, queue the collision sound and begin player state 13 with its matching pose/delay.
Retain A as the pending impact-image selector and enter the common flicflac rewind/recovery setup.
If forced motion is active, subtract twelve energy. Clear the geometry-collision flag $C2 and enter the shared rewind setup.

Mark geometry-collision flag $C2 with $FF and enter the shared recovery path, which handles a pending hazard, queues effect one, selects state thirteen and draws the step-matching pose before resetting its step counter.

Process a pending hazard, queue collision effect one and clear the stored direction's bit one. Commit candidate coordinates, select state thirteen and draw its matching pose/delay, then reset the action step.

Dispatch actor modes $F0, $F4-$F7 and $FC. Choose the death animation, transform eligible results into question-mark/revealed pickup phases, apply downward motion and floor collision, and expire the pickup after its animation cycles. Uncollected positive types add two to the Master up to $30; expired type zero subtracts four, with threshold events updating the central warning state.
Clear/hide the active sprites, print the inline GAME OVER text, wait for one hundred changes of the low tick and restore the display through $1FEE.
Inline text argument for $1CF0: screen offset $023F, followed by the zero-terminated string 'GAME OVER'. The printer resumes at $A083; ASCII [ is a font-specific display character.
Resume after the inline GAME OVER text. Count one hundred changes of low tick $3A and jump to the display-restoration entry at $1FEE.

Reset the player's transient action and geometry state for room entry, prepare collision/state geometry and persistent tile-change flags, clear active actor slots and build seven-byte scheduler entries from this room's object-directory range. Retain source pointers, respawn delays, route flags and timestamps for the subsequent allocator.

Preserve Y, copy the player coordinates into the candidate fields and query the signed room-exit rectangles without committing movement. For a matched nonnegative auxiliary state index, add the room-state base and request that state to close. Restore Y.
Retire the four actor slots, set the wave state and a displaced tick origin, initialize/clear the effects player and enable its sound-mode bit.
When at least ten low ticks have passed, advance the saved message tick and decrement the central message countdown $13C0 if nonzero.
Choose the central portrait/message image, including its timed warning alternation, and copy three rows of eight glyphs and colours into the central status area.
Enter the falling actor controller with vertical speed two.
Load downward speed four and fall through into the shared falling-actor controller at $A215. The separately traced health-threshold caller loads four itself and jumps directly to $A215.

Save the previous position, advance animation and add the supplied downward speed. Refresh bounds and test floor geometry; on contact roll back Y, clear the associated monitor flag where its contact pointer matches, and retire this actor. Otherwise stage its sprites.

Draw a random byte and return immediately unless it is below $10. On the accepted path, set actor Y to a random value one through 64 and use another random draw in the common X-position setup at $8780.
Offset 0 in pickup_bitmap_patch_offsets ($A28C-$A29D). Per-pickup offsets into the glyph mask/pattern arrays used when patching a revealed pickup bitmap in its cached sprite.
Offset 0 in pickup_bitmap_patch_patterns ($A29E-$A2F1). OR patterns applied to selected bytes of the cached pickup sprite after the matching AND mask, selecting the revealed pickup symbol.
Offset 48 in pickup_bitmap_patch_patterns ($A29E-$A2F1). OR patterns applied to selected bytes of the cached pickup sprite after the matching AND mask, selecting the revealed pickup symbol.
Offset 0 in pickup_bitmap_patch_masks ($A2F2-$A345). AND masks paired with the revealed-pickup OR patterns at $A29E.
Offset 48 in pickup_bitmap_patch_masks ($A2F2-$A345). AND masks paired with the revealed-pickup OR patterns at $A29E.
Clear two 256-byte screen ranges at $05E0 and $06E0 for an overlay message.
Select a $C0-iteration message wait and enter the shared overlay/wait routine.
Select a one-iteration message wait. Clear the message area, print its inline prompt and poll the score display and input; return X zero on timeout or $FF when input ends the wait.
Inline text argument for $1CF0: screen offset $0215, followed by the zero-terminated string 'HIGHEST SCORES'. The printer resumes at $A374; ASCII [ is a font-specific display character.
Pull the message-wait count saved before the inline prompt and fall through to the counted display/input polling helper at $A375.
Use A as the wait count, repeatedly refresh the high-score display through $3203 and poll input through $1E40. Return X zero for expiration or $FF for input.

Scan seven-byte room scheduler entries for an inactive eligible object, checking its respawn interval, disabled flags and available sprite budget. Initialize a free actor slot, call its spawn handler and either return the accepted actor or disable/defer the entry and continue. Carry set reports the end sentinel.
Jump through $20/$21. Spawn dispatch reads the pointer from object bytes 1/2; ordinary actor updates load the per-slot pointer at $12E2/$12E6.
Temporarily install the supplied actor collision-shape pointer, test its full rectangle against the player's, then restore the actor's ordinary bounds and return the overlap carry.

Select one of the five-byte attack records at $A4E7. If its rectangle overlaps the player outside doorway states, apply recoil, place an impact effect, subtract twelve energy and ten score units, then restore the active actor index.

Two five-byte directed actor attacks. Each record holds a collision-shape word, recoil mode, horizontal effect offset and vertical effect offset; the common contact routine selects offsets zero or five.
High byte of the first contact-attack collision-shape pointer in the five-byte record at $A4E7.
Recoil/direction mode of the first five-byte actor contact attack, combined with actor facing by the contact handler.
Horizontal impact offset of the first actor contact-attack record. Its sign is selected from actor facing when constructing the short effect position.
Vertical impact offset of the first five-byte actor contact attack. Following bytes begin the second record, whose collision-shape pointer and offsets have the same format.

Decrement the actor's packed recoil counter, derive a capped horizontal speed with the stored recoil direction, move and stage the actor. When the counter expires, restore the saved velocities, clear recoil/direction flags and return carry set so ordinary updates can resume.
Eight component-flag/colour values indexed by revealed pickup type after subtracting the hidden-phase offset. The pickup updater writes these into its mutable component-shape stream.
Eight alternate component-flag/colour values paired with $A547, written into the second pickup-shape field by the pickup updater.
Five-byte collision shape used when a death animation becomes an active pickup: signed top/bottom, left/right and reflection-anchor fields.
Commit the candidate player coordinates, then use the facing direction when entering the player-to-actor contact check.

Build the player's collision rectangle at the current position and call $A5F0 in contact mode. A hit subtracts ten score units, chooses recoil direction using the random byte and overlap result, and enters the player damage/recoil handler. Return carry set for a detected hit.
Use damage $0C for a selected charged piston, or four for an ordinary punch, then enter the common actor attack check.
Select damage four and enter the common actor attack rectangle check.
Select damage four for the Metalisis kick contact and enter the common actor attack-rectangle setup at $A5C9.
Select projectile attack mode and damage four. Derive the horizontal direction restriction from projectile type $84, with vertical types using the unrestricted direction marker.
Select damage six and the player's horizontal facing before entering the common actor attack check.
Use the unrestricted direction marker, build the attack rectangle from $64-$66 and shape $73, and call $A5F0. On a hit, retain the caller's attack marker in $A1; return the collision carry.

Test the supplied rectangle against four active actor slots, respecting actor mode and pickup-phase filters. Contact mode collects revealed pickups or damages the player; attack mode can reveal question-mark drops, reduce actor health, start recoil/death and award score. Continue through the slots, returning carry set when the hit count $A4 is nonzero.

Award the pickup's score and dispatch its type: zero drains active energy by $14, types 1-4 add energy to one or both characters, type five adds six laser charges and type six adds ten piston charges, capped at $63. Set the status message/sound as appropriate and retire the actor slot.

Count a hit, derive its overlap direction, update the actor's hit counter and subtract damage unless its health is $FF. A surviving actor receives recoil animation/direction and sound; a defeated actor is removed, can advance persistent object state and awards score when its origin comparison permits it.
Five actor modes matched by the damage handler when selecting a specialized hit animation frame.
Five animation cursors paired with the mode table at $A806. The damage handler requires both mode and cursor to match before changing its hit-frame state.
Replacement animation cursors written on the specialized hit cases selected by the preceding two five-entry tables.

Third entry of the five-entry hit replacement-cursor table at $A810. The defeated-object reset also uses this address as an indexed base with Y eight through eleven, reaching the separate four reset bytes at $A81A.
Five frame-delay/count values paired with the hit replacement cursors at $A810.

Four bytes read by the defeated-object path using $A812+Y with Y from $0B down through eight. That path writes them through $8F/$90 into the same record offsets, then runs its following zero-fill loop. They are separate reset data beyond the five-entry hit-animation tables.
Toggle the character index in Y and enter the six-point energy addition at $A822.
Add six to character energy $0E[Y] and clamp it to $E0 before returning.

Take a change/state index in A, clear its current state at $02C0 and scan this room's four-byte replacement records. For matching indices, find the screen destination through the shared fifty-cell pointer tables, draw the replacement tile/orientation and set its persistent flag at $0100+room-base+index. Count newly changed records in $37.
Read this room's state-flag base from $76CA and its adjacent start/end pointers from the word directory at $76B0. Return the flag base at $32 and the record interval at $20-$23.

Scan sixteen seven-byte records at $7301 for room and player-position containment. A nonnegative control applies its tile change, queues effect six and advances progress using newly changed records; a negative control marks the recharge point through $13D4. No matching activation queues effect one. Carry distinguishes a tile change from recharge/no-match paths.
Multiply state index X by eight and return its record byte offset in Y.

Link slot X to scheduler offset Y, optionally reset its mutable source record, then distribute object fields into the actor's parallel arrays using the $A9AB transfer map. Clear bounds and motion counters. When the occurrence test permits, initialize the source record's animation pointer.
Store the animation pointer from A/Y, reset the frame cursor, retain the current tick and mark the sprite data dirty. Return carry clear.

Offset 0 in actor_field_transfer_map ($A9AB-$A9C7). Twenty-nine source-field transfer offsets for the actor initializer. $FF skips a field; other values select a parallel array relative to $12D9 plus actor slot. Spawn callbacks and mutable/reset fields are handled separately.
Locate the actor's source object through its scheduler entry and write back flags, coordinates, facing and occurrence count. Clear temporary recoil/direction flag bits before saving.
Negate the actor's signed vertical velocity at $1366+X.
Negate horizontal velocity, update facing from its sign and mark the actor's sprite data dirty.

Offset 0 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 26 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 30 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 34 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 38 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 42 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 48 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 96 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Offset 144 in pickup_component_shapes ($AA25-$AAB7). Component sprite streams used by the death/revealed-pickup animations. The pickup updater patches selected flags/colours within these streams before staging them.

Twenty-eight three-byte frames for death and pickup phases: component-shape word and delay/loop flag. Sequence-entry pointers choose subsets; a delay high bit loops that sequence. The allocation ends at $AB0B, immediately before a retained executable update prefix.
Offset 48 in pickup_death_animations ($AAB8-$AB0E). Three-byte shape-pointer/delay frames for the actor death and pickup phases. Delay bit seven loops to the first frame.
Call the actor animation updater at $AD9D, then fall directly into the component-sprite staging routine at $AB0F. These three bytes are a JSR instruction, rather than another animation frame.

Read the current animation's shape pointer and actor coordinates, derive reflection from facing and flags, and call the component sprite writer at $AC42. The previous sprite-slot assignment controls whether bitmap unpacking can be skipped. Return the next free slot in $AE and restore the active actor index.

Try up to eight progressively smaller downward displacements while advancing animation. Test floor geometry and the actor's target height, rolling back blocked movement; clear the doorway mode when movement is finished, then stage its sprites.
Store the collision-shape pointer supplied in A/Y and enter the bound calculator at $ABA6.

Read signed top/bottom and left/right offsets through the actor's collision-shape pointer. Add them to its coordinates, saturate vertical bounds and reflect horizontal offsets according to facing and flags. Store the full-resolution rectangle in the actor's parallel bound arrays.
Shared entry after $ABA6 has selected the actor's collision-shape pointer in $1C/$1D. Compute saturated vertical bounds and facing-reflected full-resolution X bounds from its signed offsets.

Decode a component-shape stream through $26/$27 into secondary sprite slots up to slot four. Apply shape-relative positions, world-to-screen clipping and reflection, unpack the main and optional clipped bitmaps when dirty, set colours/flags/priority and mark each slot ready. A $FF image terminates the stream.
Reject negative attack flags, add the room-state base to A and request the state's opening path. Store a nonzero current tick in its timer at $1280+index and return carry set.

Once per tick, scan the five keyboard records at $98A6 when both joystick ports read idle. Each matching key increments its debounce counter toward three and calls its handler once on reaching three; a released key decrements the counter toward zero.

Use each actor's frame-data pointer, cursor and tick to advance its three-byte animation records. Delay is encoded in the low seven bits, with the high bit selecting a loop. A changed image marks the actor's sprite staging state dirty.
Add vertical displacement A to actor Y, then add signed horizontal displacement Y to its low/high X fields at $130A/$130E.

Enter with signed horizontal displacement in A. Add it to actor X low and extend the signed carry into X high; CMP #$80 derives the sign from A. The optional entry-carry path inspects facing but rejoins at the same comparison.

Convert the half-resolution horizontal bounds $69/$6A into full-resolution left/right coordinates, with the world's $0100 origin. Store the resulting word bounds at $6E-$71 for rectangle intersection.

Preserve Y, build the player's current collision rectangle and scan its floor group when no falling-origin Y is retained. Return carry clear for a contact found by the scanner, or set it while recording/retaining the fall state.
Save A as the landing-mode flag $77, mark $78, clear the room-entry flag $A8 and retain the player's Y in $76. Return carry set.

Scan four-byte floor records for horizontal overlap and a nearby vertical surface whose persistent gate permits contact. Snap player Y relative to that surface, or advance it by twelve when no surface is found. A landing chooses recovery based on the retained fall origin and mode; its delay grows with fall distance and is capped at $20.
Clear the current walk-phase bit, select either the special landing pose or the character's standing pose and draw it with delay three. Restore the saved Y and return carry set.
Accept candidate coordinates inside the world bounds; otherwise derive half-X and ask the room-exit search for a transition. A matched exit can invoke the route-position setter.
Copy candidate X word $61/$62 and Y $63 into player X $5C/$5E and Y $5D, then return carry clear.

Use the room's byte boundaries at $76D6 to scan six-byte exit rectangles at $729B. Mode bit six chooses the sign of eligible rectangle flags, and bit seven requests a query without moving the player. On a match retain its auxiliary byte in $9B and either return or route through its low-six-bit destination. With no match, commit candidate coordinates unless query mode suppresses it, then return carry set.

Retain candidate Y as the previous vertical origin, then use A as an entry index into four-byte records at $6C4E. Set room, X and Y, retain a relative vertical offset during flicflac, request room redraw and clear all eight sprite publication positions. A pending wave or index $25 also marks the part-ending state and redirects the entry index to zero.

Save the actor position, add signed velocities and refresh its bounds. Test horizontal and vertical geometry plus the actor's movement limits. On a blocked axis, restore its coordinate, refresh bounds and reverse that axis velocity; preserve successful movement on the other axis.
Take the pending progress amount from $C4 and enter the room-progress update at $B0FA.

Add A to this room's saturating progress byte at $0194. Scan ten seven-byte event records at $7C7C for thresholds crossed by this addition, apply their pointer-targeted byte changes and optionally publish a central status message. Preserve the caller's X.
Preserve player state $59 while invoking the geometry-hazard response at $B168, then restore that state.

When $BF is negative, choose recoil direction, subtract ten score units and eight energy, clear the hazard marker and select forced motion. A matching progress-event pointer can also select a central warning message.
Store direction/mode A in $BD, set forced-motion count $BE to two and queue effect eight.

Check the interaction's attack-mask and persistent prerequisites, subtract the attack's low-six-bit damage from its retained strength and play a hit effect. A final hit sets its persistent flag, applies the room tile change, awards score/progress and starts a timed impact animation at the object's coordinates. Return carry set when the attack type is refused.

Scan eight seventeen-byte moving-platform records for this room. Draw the current platform through $B2BD, then fill the remaining vertical span with the three-cell extension glyph/colour templates while staying inside the playfield.
Scan eight seventeen-byte moving-platform records and redraw those whose room equals $3C through $B2BD. Unlike $B24B, this entry does not fill their extension spans.

Calculate screen/colour pointers from the platform's half-step position and authored base offset. Choose one of two twelve-byte glyph/colour frames from its position parity, draw up to four three-cell rows and clip the writes to the playfield.

After at least four low ticks, scan the eight moving platforms in this room. Use player contact, character, change-flash and flicflac state to choose or inhibit vertical motion between each record's limits. Update three linked collision lines and redraw the platform. When the player stands on it, move the player and staged player sprite slices by the same Y displacement.
Offset 0 in room_animated_glyph_a ($B4D4-$B4F3). Four eight-byte glyph frames copied to world character $34 in rooms five and six.
Offset 0 in room_animated_glyph_b ($B4F4-$B503). Two eight-byte glyph frames copied to world character $35 alongside the four-frame animation.

Offset 0 in retained_digit_bitmaps ($B504-$B5B3). Eleven sixteen-byte single-bit images: digits zero through nine and a left/right arrow pair. Rendering the bytes as eight pixels by sixteen rows identifies the images. Their role beyond retained graphics is open; ordinary status digits use the separate $2000 character set.

Offset 48 in retained_digit_bitmaps ($B504-$B5B3). Eleven sixteen-byte single-bit images: digits zero through nine and a left/right arrow pair. Rendering the bytes as eight pixels by sixteen rows identifies the images. Their role beyond retained graphics is open; ordinary status digits use the separate $2000 character set.

Offset 96 in retained_digit_bitmaps ($B504-$B5B3). Eleven sixteen-byte single-bit images: digits zero through nine and a left/right arrow pair. Rendering the bytes as eight pixels by sixteen rows identifies the images. Their role beyond retained graphics is open; ordinary status digits use the separate $2000 character set.

Offset 144 in retained_digit_bitmaps ($B504-$B5B3). Eleven sixteen-byte single-bit images: digits zero through nine and a left/right arrow pair. Rendering the bytes as eight pixels by sixteen rows identifies the images. Their role beyond retained graphics is open; ordinary status digits use the separate $2000 character set.
Render laser charge $17 and piston charge $18 in their two status-field positions through the shared numeric writer, preserving X.

Form the signed horizontal separation between the actor rectangle and the supplied rectangle by summing their left/right bounds and subtracting the other pair, retaining the intermediate carries on the stack. Return the low difference in Y and high difference in A.

After at least five low ticks, walk this room's state range. Opening states approach their target position; closing states approach zero. A closing door with a collision record checks the player and four actor rectangles, reopening and postponing its timer when blocked. Mark changed states for the display updater.

For each state whose redraw bit is set, clear that bit and read its eight-byte descriptor. Adjust linked wall-collision records for the current opening position, then draw the descriptor's glyph rows and colours. Certain types select a pattern from $6A92; fully open types either copy the neighboring cell or blank the row.
Twelve target opening positions indexed by room-state type. Room geometry preparation copies the selected value into the runtime target array at $1260.
Twelve glyph-row widths indexed by state type. The changed-state renderer uses the selected width for its pattern offset and row-copy loops.
Select forward bitmap orientation and enter $B84C to stage a short impact at half-resolution X and Y supplied by the caller.

Refuse with carry set while $7F denotes an active projectile. Otherwise stage sprite zero at the supplied position, unpack image $5F into its cache, select colour/flags and scenery priority, and retain a nonzero low tick in $13BB for the four-tick expiry helper. Return carry clear.
Scan this room's state range. For a state with a nonzero timer and opening flag $40, compare elapsed low ticks with $96; once reached, request its closing path through $87B6.

When $7F is active, run the impact animation if phase $80 is nonzero; otherwise move the shot using its type and elapsed ticks, test screen/room/actor collisions and publish sprite slot zero. A vertical upward shot can change to the downward type after impact. Update its cached bitmap, colour and scenery priority before marking the slot ready.
Four upward displacement magnitudes selected from elapsed low-tick count, capped by the projectile updater before lookup.
Four downward displacement magnitudes, paired with the upward table and selected by projectile type.
Four horizontal displacement magnitudes indexed by the projectile's capped elapsed-tick count.
Six sprite image indices indexed by projectile type: the paired horizontal, downward and upward direction variants.
Six reflection flags paired with the projectile image/type table at $BA28.
Six half-resolution horizontal offsets added to the geometry-clamped projectile contact X when placing its short impact sprite. The projectile type selects the entry.
Six vertical offsets added to the clamped contact Y when placing a projectile's short impact sprite, paired with $BA34.

Copy candidate coordinates into the geometry workspace, derive horizontal direction from old versus candidate X and call the horizontal collision resolver. Copy any clamped result back to the candidate fields and retain the collision carry.
Copy current player coordinates into the geometry workspace, use facing for the scan direction and X for its collision-shape index, then enter $BA76.

Form the supplied pose rectangle and select the left/right collision list from the incoming carry. On contact, retain an optional hazard flag/pointer, compensate for the facing-dependent pose offset and clamp the workspace X to the contact boundary. Return carry set for contact.

Copy candidate coordinates and the old player Y into the geometry workspace, run the vertical resolver and propagate clamped coordinates back. A hazardous contact records its direction/pointer; a downward contact can update the retained landing Y.

Set carry for the upward scan, copy current coordinates, choose shape X and use the common vertical collision path. A contact with the hazard flag records the player's opposite facing for its later response.
Clear carry for the downward scan and share the coordinate setup and common vertical geometry resolver at $BB2A.
Set bit seven on direction A in $BF and retain the current collision record's fourth-byte address in $C0/$C1 for the later player response.
Compare old Y $67 with candidate Y $66 to choose vertical scan direction, then enter the common rectangle resolver at $BB65.

Build the workspace pose rectangle and scan floor or ceiling records according to the saved carry. Skip disabled persistent gates. Downward motion additionally checks that the old bottom was above the candidate surface. On contact, clamp Y using the pose offset, return its contact pointer in $A5/$A6 and return A zero for a floor or $FF for a ceiling, with carry set. No contact returns carry clear.

In rooms five and six, wait until the low tick difference from $13B7 reaches four, then advance $13C2. With I/O hidden, copy one of four eight-byte glyphs from $B4D4 into $09A0 and one of two from $B4F4 into $09A8. Restore I/O visibility before returning.

Take a shape index in A and read its shared descriptor through $1C48. Wait until the staged player slots are free, place layered bitmap pieces in sprite slots 5 and 6 using the player's position/facing, unpack their cache images and optional lower vertical images, and apply descriptor colours. A flagged descriptor can add a weapon piece in slot 7 unless $A0 suppresses it. Apply hit-flash colours and sprite-priority checks, handle the pending effect at $9E, then mark slots 5-7 ready for publication.
RTS ending the layered player renderer. The impact-horizontal table uses this address as a base for nonzero selectors; selector one reads the following byte at $BE44.

Offset 0 in player_impact_horizontal_offsets ($BE44-$BE55). Eighteen horizontal offsets for pending player impact selectors one through eighteen. The lookup uses base $BE43, overlapping the preceding RTS at unused selector zero, and reverses the offset for reflected facing.

Twenty vertical offsets for pending impact selector $9E, added to player Y before creating the short-impact sprite. Byte zero also supplies the horizontal offset for selector nineteen through the overlapping horizontal lookup base at $BE43.

Take a secondary bitmap index in A and sprite slot in X. Select the cache destination using $16ED[X]-$03A0[X], form a relative-word directory pointer at $C838+2*A and enter the shared packed-bitmap decoder. Preserve the caller's Y in $7B and return the slot index in X with carry set.
As $BE6A, but add two to the cache destination index before unpacking. This chooses the alternate cached slice for a sprite slot.
Take a main bitmap index in X and destination cache index in A. Form the directory-word pointer at $C73C+2*X, preserve Y at $7B and enter the shared decoder at $BEC1.

Decode the directory word addressed by $1E/$1F into the 63-byte sprite cache at $2800+64*A, with I/O hidden during the copy. A zero high byte fills the image with $FF. Otherwise the low fifteen bits give an offset from $C73C; $C8 escapes a literal and $C9-$CF emit one through seven zeros. $7C selects horizontal reflection, whose bit-group width comes from directory bit fifteen. Restore Y and the processor port before returning.
Low address byte of the forward packed-stream LDA at $BF02. Decoder setup patches it and its high byte from the selected directory stream pointer.

High address byte of the forward packed-stream lookup at $BF02, patched to the stream pointer before decoding. The loop interprets literals, $C8 escape and one-to-seven-zero runs until 63 output bytes have been written.
Low operand byte of the escaped-literal LDA at $BF1F, patched together with the ordinary forward source.
High address operand byte of the escaped-literal LDA at $BF1F. It is patched with the same source pointer as the ordinary forward packed-stream lookup.

Reflect each decoded three-byte sprite row: reverse the byte order through the stack and translate each byte through $1000 or $1100. Carry from the directory's high flag selects two-bit-group or single-bit reversal. Runs and escaped bytes use the same packed format as the forward decoder; stop after 63 destination bytes.
Low operand byte of the reflected stream LDY at $BF59, paired with its patched high byte at $BF5B.

High address byte of the reflected packed-stream lookup at $BF59. The decoder patches this and the escaped-byte source from the same stream pointer, reverses each row through the stack and applies the selected reflection lookup table.
Low operand byte of the reflected escaped-literal LDY at $BF90, paired with $BF92.
High operand byte of the escaped-literal LDY at $BF90, patched together with the ordinary reflected packed-stream source.
Low address byte of the reflection lookup at $BF94. Setup writes zero here and selects page $10/$11 through its high operand byte.
High byte of the lookup at $BF94, patched to $10 or $11 to select reversal of two-bit groups or individual bits. Each result is pushed while the decoder reverses the three-byte row.

Select four room-specific collision groups from the tables at $6CE2, $6DCE, $6EFA and $6FD2, storing pointers at $85-$8C.
